newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-RBA to watch wages in rates decision - Costello.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-RBA to watch wages in rates decision - Costello.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello said on Thursday the Reserve Bank would take wages data into account in any decision on official interest rates.
"They'll take into account wages figures and they'll make decisions accordingly," Costello told Australian Broadcasting Corp radio.

Average Weekly Ordinary Time Earnings (AWOTE) data for the three months to May is due to be released at 0130 GMT on Wednesday. Economists are on average forecasting quarterly wages growth of 0.9 percent and annual growth of 4.1 percent.
Economists see Thursday's data as the last possible hurdle to a fifth rate cut in this cycle.

Earlier, Costello said unemployment had to come down and that the government was leaving no stone unturned to do that. "We are working on the long term solutions in terms of economic growth. We are fixing the industrial relations system," he said.
He said he would not set a unemployment rate target.
"Unemployment has to come down," he said, adding however that setting a target could limit any government's ambitions.

The current 8.5 percent unemployment rate coupled with data released on Wednesday showing annual consumer price inflation of 0.3 percent are seen prompting the rate cut if wages growth continues to moderate.
